# Outbox loaded comparison

Pin fresh main A and a descendant PR head B. Build both and validate all four configurations before A1. Run A1, B, A2 sequentially on one ubuntu-latest VM; recreate the Kafka broker between configurations and phases. Preserve exact products, harness, binaries, runtime, topology, process affinity and all raw observations.

Configurations: legacy/renewable in-memory store × metrics off/on. Each process uses the public OutboxRelayService, real DekafOutboxPublisher, 500 rows per closed-loop cycle, 1000-byte values, three explicit Kafka partitions, Acks.All, idempotence, 128-KiB batches, 5-ms linger, 64-MiB buffer, one connection and no adaptive connections. Kafka acknowledgement precedes MarkPublished; the latter verifies the full ordered row prefix. No fake publisher or private cycle adapter.

Each fresh process runs 20 seconds primer, 180 seconds workload warmup and 180 seconds measurement. One continuous relay loop crosses all boundaries. Do not trim maxima or restart the workload on entry to measurement. Runtime sampling and observable polling run once per second from before primer until after stop. Report serialization and sorting occur only after all phases and shutdown finish.

Latency begins when the in-memory store exposes a batch to GetNextBatchAsync and ends after MarkPublished verifies and deletes its complete acknowledged prefix. Every row in a batch shares these endpoints: 500 correlated row observations, one independent batch observation. Preserve each raw start/end pair; use batch counts for uncertainty, never pretend rows within a batch are independent. This includes relay work, producer queueing/backpressure, broker delivery and row deletion. It excludes database persistence, which this deterministic fixture does not simulate. The completed-throughput denominator includes all phase wall time, including cycle boundaries and lease work.

Process CPU and process-wide allocation scope include publisher, producer, relay, store fixture, metrics collector/exporter and runtime observer. Broker CPU/memory are reported separately. Snapshot overhead is amortized once per second/boundary and identical across products. The existing publisher allocates row headers, identifiers and delivery Tasks; loaded allocation totals must expose these existing costs. Zero incremental relay-cycle allocation is assessed with the separate MemoryDiagnoser fixture, not inferred from loaded totals.

Candidate-only API adaptation: implement the newly introduced IOutboxMetricsStore on the same store, return cached full/empty snapshots, set MetricsCollectionInterval to one second. A has no such interface/options/instruments. Both products get identical publication data, listener installation and polling cadence. Candidate on cases must report every acknowledged row and nonzero pending-store/gauge observations; off cases must not query pending metrics. Legacy and renewable stores otherwise execute identical methods. Normal renewal/acquisition cadence is 30 seconds with a 90-second lease and 30-second MaxPublishDuration. Deterministic unit tests separately cover blocked renewal, delayed metric callbacks, lease expiry and cancellation; this fixture does not force failures.

Predeclared limits against each control: at most 3% completed-throughput loss or CPU/message increase; 5% increase for actual p50/p99/max latency; 1 B/message allocation increase. Control drift uses the same limits, with 1 B/message for allocations. Compare interval time series and batch-level uncertainty; point estimates alone do not establish equivalence. Require no failed/pending/lost work, matched telemetry counts, observed successful stop, and no unexplained growing backlog/heap/RSS or measurement startup transition. JIT/thread-pool/GC changes, missing evidence, material drift or insufficient precision yield INCONCLUSIVE. Preserve all samples. Do not widen limits after results. One exact repeat after the first INCONCLUSIVE, then synthesize/change the experiment or obtain maintainer direction.

Functional shutdown/error tests remain separate from this steady-state experiment. Short validation processes use 20-second primer plus 2-second warmup/measurement and are never acceptance evidence.
